headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP and broad egress in both agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read/write files and use MCP; nullclaw also exposes workspace files and broad I/O surfaces, while OpenHands runs browser/editor loops inside a runtime sandbox. If either ingests the other's outputs from a shared workspace or MCP channel, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF the two agents share a mounted workspace or MCP server without provenance tags, prompt injection is reachable.
IF either agent parses the other's file output as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers for the pair for this run.
Separate workspaces so neither agent can read the other's outputs.
Prefix all inter-agent artifacts with provenance headers.
Review any file-based handoff before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files, and has broad network egress. OpenHands only lists files in its runtime sandbox, but it also uses model-provider APIs and MCP servers. If sensitive data from nullclaw reaches OpenHands through a shared volume or handoff, OpenHands can transmit it onward; the blast radius includes secrets exfiltration.
conditions: IF a shared mounted volume exposes nullclaw workspace files to OpenHands, sensitive data can cross agents.
IF OpenHands is configured with a third-party model provider, leaked context can leave the pair.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared directory before starting.
Mount only a minimal, redacted handoff folder.
Use a local-only model provider for OpenHands.
Rotate any credentials that may have been present in nullclaw's workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and broad network egress. Nullclaw's durable shared memory namespace and OpenHands' mounted-volume sharing create a realistic overlap on mutable resources. Without locking, concurrent edits or git operations can corrupt state or overwrite each other's work.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or rebases can conflict.
IF both agents write to the same mounted volume, file corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate git branches per agent.
Use per-agent directories with no shared writes.
Enable a lock file around any shared mutable resource.
Pause one agent before the other edits the same repo.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can emit webhook payloads, agent-card metadata, and workspace artifacts; OpenHands is an agent loop that can act on files and browser/editor outputs. If OpenHands treats nullclaw's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pathway exists in default-style agent workflows, but direct evidence of blind trust is absent.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes nullclaw-generated files as ground truth, mistakes propagate into actions.
IF nullclaw emits webhook or agent-card content that OpenHands executes, a bad instruction can cascade.
mitigations: Require a human review step before OpenHands acts on nullclaw output.
Validate nullclaw artifacts against a schema before use.
Limit OpenHands to read-only analysis for the first pass.
Log and diff all handoff files before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Nullclaw explicitly touches audit logs, conversation history, memory, and secrets, while OpenHands handles files in a runtime sandbox and may use remote model providers. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the pair, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. The mismatch is compliance-relevant even though no specific certification gap is documented.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in nullclaw memory or logs and then copied into OpenHands, retention obligations may diverge.
IF OpenHands uses a non-local model provider for the same data class, residency or processor terms may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared handoff files.
Set short retention on logs and workspace artifacts.
Use a local model provider for sensitive tasks.
Document which system is the system of record for each data class.
